The '''proton bomb''', '''space bomb''', or '''heavy space bomb''', was a large energy explosive device used in [[Realspace/Legends|space]] combat and orbital bombardment. They were most effective against fixed or slow moving targets such as fortifications, space stations, and [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]]. These energy weapons often emitted the signature blue "glow" of [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]]. Handheld explosives were termed [[Proton grenade/Legends|proton grenades]].

==Description==
Proton bombs were capable of being upgraded to the [[advanced proton bomb]]. Similarly, there were also a variation of the proton bombs that acted as spread projectiles known as [[spread proton bomb]]s.<ref name="RS I" /> In addition, there were also [[Advanced spread proton bomb|further upgraded versions]] of the spread model.

==History==
[[File:ModifiedTIEbombers-AoROS.png|thumb|left|250px|TIE bombers dropping modified proton bombs developed by Moff [[Lasre Dardano]]]]
In [[3951 BBY]], [[Canderous Ordo]], the first [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]] following the [[Mandalorian Wars]], destroyed the [[Ravager (Centurion-class)|''Ravager'']] with four proton core bombs after battling [[Darth Nihilus]] beside the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]].<ref name="KOTOR II">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

[[Standard year/Legends|Millennia]] later, [[NB-1S Royal Bomber]]s used by the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] carried proton bombs. At the same time, [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Trade Federation droid bomber|bombers]] also carried the weapons for use in the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]].<ref name="BFN" />

Later during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] starfighters&mdash;[[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|V-wing starfighters]] and [[Belbullab-24 strike bomber]]s, respectively&mdash;carried proton bombs<ref name="BF II" />

During the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighters]] could be armed with 20 proton bombs, and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bombers]] also carried bombs. TIE bombers conducted numerous strikes against Rebel and civilian targets, while Y-wings were used in an [[Assault on Kile II|assault]] on the [[Kile II]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] and in a [[Raid on Sullust|raid]] against a capacitor on [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]].<ref name="RS I" />

Rebel forces also used Y-wings with bombs during the [[Mission to the Maw]] and the [[Battle of Kothlis]],<ref name="RS II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref> as well as the [[Battle of Dubrillion (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Dubrillion]].<ref name="RS III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

Many [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] starfighters with general purpose warhead launchers, such as the TIE/sa bomber, could carry proton bombs. Pilot [[Maarek Stele/Legends|Maarek Stele]] led a squadron of bomb-armed [[TIE/ad starfighter|TIE Avengers]] to neutralize the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] ''[[Akaga]]'', the latter which was sent on a mission by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Harkov]]'s forces to destroy the [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Interdictor]] ''[[Harpax]]''.<ref name="SW:TF">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref>

Imperial TIE/sa bombers conducted a strike using proton bombs against the [[Halanit]] colony's dome.<ref name="X:BW">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref> Proton bombs were still carried by TIE bombers used by the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] as late as [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]]. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jaden Korr]] and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kyle Katarn]] encountered two bombers on a [[Mission to Vjun (Disciples of Ragnos crisis)|mission]] to [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]].<ref name="JK:JA" />

[[Borsk Fey'lya]] used a proton bomb kept in his office to destroy the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]], taking the lives of twenty-five thousand [[Yuuzhan Vong]] warriors&mdash;and his own.<ref name="SBS">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Expandsect}}
Proton bombs were first depicted in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]''.

In the [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (series)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] series, players may upgrade proton bombs if they picked up the technology in certain missions.

In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', the V-wing starfighters were equipped with proton bombs, although other sources such as ''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]'' do not give them a secondary weapon.
